newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriots protest against British military exercise.
newsitem.headline: Cypriots protest against British military exercise.

text.p: Twelve Cypriot environmentalists were detained on Monday when they entered a firing range on the island's remote Akamas peninsula trying to stop British military exercises there, police said.

"We do not want to arrest them. It is for their own protection," police spokesman Glafcos Xenos told Reuters. The demonstrators, members of local environment groups, were later released without charge.
Another smaller group of activists emerged from hiding in the thick vegetation where they had spent their morning to protest against the British military's use of the area as a firing range.
At least two people, including a member of parliament, had still not emerged in late afternoon, when British soldiers started live exercises in the area, witnesses said.
The activists, who camped in the north western peninsula overnight, had scattered into the woods earlier Monday when anti-riot police appeared on the scene.
The troops, from the base of Episkopi on the island's southern coast, are due to leave the region on Friday.
Soldiers from two military bases which Britain has retained on the island since independence in 1960 are allowed to train in the Akamas for up to 70 days a year.
Environmental groups have called for the peninsula to be declared a national park. Britain argues the military exercises protect the environment by keeping developers at bay.
Last week a parliamentary committee issued a report urging the government to take measures to stop the exercises, which have been the subject of controversy for years.

"The Foreign Ministry is engaged in a dialogue with the British military authorities in Cyprus to find another area to exercise outside of the Akamas," Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told reporters.
